text:
maya: Heads up — nightly TP training shows a 3-4x tail in all-reduce latency after yesterday's kernel-selection change, starts ~10:30pm PDT. cc @javier @sophia

javier: saw the same on the dashboard, median token throughput OK but tail jumps on step boundaries. correlated with smaller comm chunk sizes (microbatching change).

sophia: can you paste a short trace? suspect ring vs tree decision is flipping for small messages and hurting startup.

maya: here’s the nvtx snippet from the profiler (trimmed):

```
NVTX: step 1234
allreduce start -> 0.48 ms
ring send chunk 0 -> 0.22 ms
ring recv chunk 0 -> 0.21 ms
allreduce end -> 0.49 ms
kernel exec -> 0.18 ms
-- repeated many small allreduce calls (~48KB each)
```

loan: perf-bot flagged a regression on the kernel-selector commit that introduced a bias toward fused-kernels for >256KB, but it looks like the selector also changed the threshold for small messages.

perf-bot: Regression alert: commit 9f2cde changed kernel heuristic. 90th p90 all-reduce latency increased from 0.6ms -> 2.1ms for 32-64 KB payloads.

javier: that matches. Previously tree-algo was selected for <128KB and ring for bigger, now the switch is around 64KB and the fused path has higher setup cost for tiny fragments.

maya: KV cache behavior complicates this — warm KV cache causes lots of tiny updates for prompt-prefix reuse, which produces many small allreduces instead of fewer bigger ones. observed increase in #allreduce ops per step from 8 -> 28.

sophia: two quick repros to run locally:
1) nccl-tests microbench (binary we use):
```
./all_reduce_perf -b 65536 -e 65536 -n 200 --msgsize 49152
```
2) stress with KV updates enabled (local driver) to reproduce high op count.

loan: also try forcing tree algorithm to confirm delta: export NCCL_ALGO=tree; re-run same microbench. If latency collapses, we know ring startup cost is the culprit for this msgshape.

maya: I ran the forced-tree test on the same nodes: p50 ~0.6ms, p95 ~0.9ms. With default selector: p50 ~0.7ms, p95 ~2.3ms. So tree is much better for our median msgshape.

javier: kernel-selection patch should add a gating rule: if median_msg_size < 128KB or ops_per_step > 16 -> prefer tree/fragment-aggregation. That would avoid picking the fused path with large setup overhead.

sophia: agree. Also consider a lightweight coalescing window in the batching heuristics: if we see many small KV updates within a 10ms window, coalesce them into larger allreduce ops before issuing. Tradeoff is slight added latency for first token but big tail improvement.

maya: proposed quick mitigation: rollback the selector change on nightly cluster and enable coalescing window 8ms for KV cache paths. Can we test the rollback on canary?

loan: I can push a canary rollout. Two steps: revert selector heuristic in runtime-config and set coalescing window flag. I'll schedule at 3am PST (low traffic).

perf-bot: Suggested test matrix to run post-rollout:
- all_reduce_perf msgsize sweep: 16KB, 32KB, 48KB, 64KB, 128KB
- real TP job with KV warm/cold toggles (10 runs each)
- trace collection with NVTX and comm timeline

javier: add a kernel-level metric: count of allreduce ops and avg msgsize per step to the perf dashboard so we can alert when ops_per_step > 12.

sophia: long-term: update kernel selection to be model-aware (prefix reuse => high small-op ratio) and consult KV cache telemetry before picking algorithm. also consider a hybrid fallback: start ring but if we detect hot small-fragment pattern, flip to tree for next N steps.

maya: thanks — I'll attach the full profiler tarball to the ticket and open a short PR for the selector gate.

loan: filing canary rollout, PR link will be in the ticket.

sophia: :thumbsup: if we get stable p95 under 1ms for the small msg shapes we're good.

maya: closing loop, will report results after the 3am canary and post perf graphs.
